messages:
oliver: Heads up — consensus runner is red after the quantized-v2 judge bring-up. tie_rate jumped to ~27% on simp-bench, which is ... surprising. Repro locally with --quantize=8.

sam: ugh. any obvious stack traces? can you paste the runner log?

oliver: pasted below — seems like the arbiter step sometimes gets an empty candidate list and reduce_votes returns null. happens ~1/20 runs.

```
# simplified stack
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"runner/eval_loop.py\", line 342, in run_task
    result = arbiter.reduce_votes(candidates)
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable
```

maya: @oliver did you try forcing fp16 on the judge model (no quant) to see if it's q-specific? also curious if this is a data race (KV cache) or a logic edgecase in tie handling. :thinking_face:

oliver: I did fp16 — no failures. It only appears with int8 quantization and only on short-context prompts (<= 64 tokens). Not every run.

zach: the CI nightly had 2 flakey consensus failures last week too; might be same root. CI config uses batch_size=64 which could stress batching path.

sam: can you try reproducing with SSH to a dedicated node and set DEBUG=runner:arbiter and disable batching? if it disappears that's a strong signal.

oliver: will try. quick hack: added a guard in reduce_votes() to return [] when candidates is None and logged context. Patch attached in my branch for now — not a fix, but avoids crash.

ci-bot: nightly-evals/2026-03-19 finished — 2 failing tests: eval/consensus_flaky (see logs) — https://ci.redwood-internal/jobs/3321/logs

maya: long-term we should add an explicit tie-breaker policy before reduce_votes: deterministic fallback that samples by model_confidence then by lexical order. That avoids arbitrary nondeterminism across quant modes. propose: 1) filter empties, 2) sort by confidence desc, 3) if confidence within eps then pick lowest hash(candidate).

zach: agree. we also need to add a unit test that simulates quant noise: perturb logits by +/- eps and assert stable winner under the tie policy. I can add to eval-runner tests.

sam: action items: oliver — repro with batching off and post logs (by EOD). zach — add tie-breaker test & CI gating. maya — write short RFC for deterministic tie policy (include hash choice rationale). I'll open a tracking ticket.

oliver: repro succeeded on a no-batch node. failure only when batching enabled and quantized. attaching minimal repro script snippet: 

```
# repro.sh
python -m runner.eval_task --model judge-v2-quant --quantize 8 --batching on --seed 42 --prompt-file tiny_prompts.json
```

sam: nice, that points to batching+quantization interaction. likely kernel ordering or shared buffer. zach can you try a fast diff on batching codepath?

zach: on it. also adding a lightweight integration test to CI that toggles batching on/off for judge bring-ups. probably we should gate deploys of quantized judges until this test is stable.

maya: also a reminder to document the tie-breaker in the eval dashboard so downstream owners know why a particular answer was chosen when scores are near-equal.

oliver: thanks — will keep thread updated. patch to avoid crash merged to staging to unblock CI, but marking as hotfix + follow-up RFC. :white_check_mark:
